newsitem.title: USA: Levitt calls for ethics in muni, other markets.
newsitem.headline: Levitt calls for ethics in muni, other markets.

text.p: SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt on Tuesday said that there is an important place for ethics in the securities market, particularly in places like the "pay-to-play" culture of the municipal securities arena.

Speaking at a celebration of the 300th anniversary of New York City's Trinity Church, Levitt said that a few weeks before he took the helm at the Securities and Exchange Commission in 1993, he was stunned by a conversation he had with three young municipal bond brokers.

"They worked in the municipal bond deparatment of two major firms," Levitt said. "One of them commented that the only way he was able to survive in the municipal bond business was by buying tables at political fundraising dinners, or by making contributions to officeholders in a position to award lucrative underwriting contracts," Levitt said.
The brokers said the practice, known as pay-to-play, was "common" in the municipal arena, Levitt said.
"How terrible, that even the newest entrants into this very vital part of the securities business were being assimilated into this culture of pay-to-play," he said.

"Little wonder that confidence in government is at such a low ebb today. This experience convinced me to try to change the practice," said Levitt, who was a lightning rod behind Wall Street's decision in 1994 to sign a voluntary ban on political contributions.
Levitt noted that the Association of the Bar of the City of New York has proposed its own rule curbing pay-to-play by bond lawyers.
"What a positive statement it would be if the lawyers were to raise themselves to the same standard of ethical conduct as bond dealers," Levitt said.
